# Unused continuation indents

Original OPC/XML fixture generated by `tools/unused_indent_fixture.py`, exported
by the reference application on 2026-09-18 without saving the source. The reference
hashes identify the exact tested source and PDF. The PNG is a 96 DPI PDF render.

A 300-twip table column contains empty, one-character and one-space paragraphs
with a 720-twip left indent and matching hanging indent. Their first line has
room; a hypothetical continuation does not. A fourth row has a valid 120-twip
continuation indent. A body paragraph similarly has a 10,000-twip left/hanging
pair, placing only its unused continuation outside the page.

The reference application renders each case as one line on a single page. The browser now does too.
The empty paragraph still contributes height and has a caret location. General
row/line metrics differ between the browser and the reference application; this is not an exact pixel match.
No specification divergence was identified: ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.1.12 applies
the hanging offset to the first line. The defect was eager validation of an
unused continuation line, not an incorrect indent value in the source.

Tests retain errors for an invalid first line and for actual wrapped/manual
continuations with no writing space. The fixture opens editable; body editing,
reopen, unchanged package parts and exact undo are covered in unit/browser tests.
